checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md:4–48; VERIFICATION.md; verify.py (inspected, not executed). Independent bounded replay: Prüfer sequences for every labelled tree of orders 1–5, enumeration of proper colorings and legal one-coordinate moves, and breadth-first search from (c,even) to (c,odd) in the parity double cover for each c. All 1,1,3,16,125 cases agree with the predicted odd girth. The all-order proof is the height/sweep derivation above.
correctness.rationale: A proper named coloring lifts to integer heights on a tree once a root lift is fixed, since every edge color difference has a unique representative in {-1,1}. A legal recoloring at a nonisolated vertex means its neighbors all have the third color, hence the height there can and must move by 2 in absolute value, with the sign preserving unit slopes. The one-vertex case allows either sign. A closed walk restores all edge differences, so all coordinates shift by a common multiple of 3, which is a multiple of 6 by parity. If the shift is 6q, summing the coordinate changes yields L>=3n*|q| and L congruent to 3n*q modulo 2. This forbids odd walks for even n and gives the lower bound for odd n. In a sweep ordered by descending height, each neighbor currently has height one less at the time of the move; lowering every height by 2 in that order is legal. Three sweeps give the necessary 3n-step closed walk, whose minimal odd length implies simplicity for odd n. A leaf can always be moved to the color different from both the old and pending neighbor colors, proving connectedness by induction. Sum of colors modulo 3 is a proper coloring; combined with the parity result and existence of edges this proves the claimed chromatic numbers. The one- and two-vertex graphs are a triangle and a hexagon. For n>=3 there are two nonadjacent leaves yielding independent moves and a square; a triangle would need to vary only a single unconstrained coordinate, impossible with a neighbor. Maximum-independent-set moves exactly coincide with recolorings because a second token in any triangle is illegal. The count follows from independent choices away from a rooted vertex and the probability 2^(1-d) that its neighbors all agree; dividing directed moves by two gives the edge formula (the singleton is direct). Connectedness gives the stated graph cycle rank.
residual_risks: The independent finite check concerns only orders 1–5; it is not an all-order certificate. Frozen verify.py:90–96 has four larger inputs per order, not four distinct isomorphism types: its first and third are both paths. The supplementary script's claimed output was not independently rerun.

evidence: Asgarli et al. Lemma 2.1 describes compatible labelings up to uniform shifts by 3. Lemma 2.5 realizes every compatible labeling as a walk of length its L1 norm, with each vertex toggled monotonically as specified. Classical 3-recolorability reachability abstracts do not supply a cycle theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known realization lemma is stronger than existence of a shortest path; the endpoint choices f=g are permitted and give exactly the closed witness for the first nonzero uniform label. General algorithmic reachability is not the basis of the negative judgment.

evidence: For an arbitrary walk, sum the prior signed toggle labels to get h. On an edge uv let d be the representative in {-1,1} of c(u)-c(v). Each toggle at an endpoint changes d by -2 times the signed differential toggle at u minus v; all other toggles leave d unchanged. Thus 2(h(u)-h(v))=d_initial-d_final. For a closed walk, h is therefore constant, and its entries are multiples of 3 by endpoint congruence. Conversely the constant label 3 is (f,f)-compatible, so Lemma 2.5 realizes it in 3n moves.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For h=3q the number of moves is at least ||h||_1=3n*|q| and is congruent to sum h=3n*q modulo 2 because every toggle contributes +1 or -1. The prior lemmas thus give both parity and the sharp length by direct specialization and counting. The new sweep is an elementary alternative witness proof, not a distinct invariant beyond this implication.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A move in a maximum-independent-set triangle is the same recoloring, and an odd cycle exists iff an odd closed walk does. Translating from height differences to signed counts does not create a new graph invariant or a new walk mechanism.

originality.rationale: The all-tree diameter theorem by itself does not determine odd girth. But its primary source supplies the stronger walk-realization lemma for every compatible signed labeling, including nonzero constant labels from a coloring to itself, as well as the uniform-shift description and signed toggles. The odd-girth/parity statement is a direct corollary of those actual lemmas and the elementary parity of signed counts, not just an analogy with a prior lifting method. This does not assert that the odd-girth formula is printed in the prior work.
residual_risks: The classical reachability article was accessible only at abstract level. The negative judgment rests on verified all-tree walk realization and explicit implication, not unavailable text, same-day chronology or a novelty search miss.

value.rationale: The coexistence of squares and large odd girth is a natural feature worth recording, but the exact odd-girth and bipartiteness classification are immediate walk-label corollaries of the already stronger all-tree realization result. The ordinary-girth cases use independent leaf moves and the elementary triangle obstruction; the remaining chromatic and graph counts either follow directly or are known. No distinct nonmechanically implied structural invariant survives in this record as a finding.
residual_risks: The result is mathematically sound and could be useful as an explicit corollary or alternate proof; the value decision addresses the submitted independent finding.
